A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PORRL framework. Their complete main texts, equations, algorithm displays and appendices support comparison despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: v1 presents algorithms, theoretical guarantees and analytical examples, including the reward-machine construction in Appendix A.5, but no original empirical results.

after.justification: v2 remains theoretical, including its combination-lock analysis. References to experiments in a process-supervision preprint do not report original experiments in this paper.

M1.justification: v2 adds a model-free PORRL approach using GOLF and joint, model-realizable Q-function classes, alongside the retained model-based algorithms. Assumption 1 broadens known reward functions to known reward-function classes, and the least-squares confidence radius is revised.

E1.justification: Neither version evaluates datasets or conducts sampled task evaluations. The revised combination-lock scenarios are mathematical constructions.

E2.justification: Neither version reports empirical baseline comparisons. Expanded comparisons with GOLF and P-OMLE concern theoretical guarantees.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental splits, training budgets or testing protocols. The added PAC objective and policy-selection argument are theoretical developments.

E4.justification: No empirical ablations, robustness tests or error analyses are added. The dense-versus-sparse combination-lock comparison establishes mathematical dimension separations, assessed under T1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experimental runs, seeds, error bars or significance tests. Changes to theoretical confidence bounds belong to the algorithm and theory.

E6.justification: Neither version contains empirical result entries. Changes concern regret bounds, sample-complexity guarantees and analytical examples rather than measured performance.

T1.justification: v2 adds regret-to-PAC lemmas and sample-complexity corollaries, the HABE dimension, and a new GOLF regret analysis. Proposition 1 and Appendix F replace v1's specialized reward-machine argument with dense/sparse-feedback dimension comparisons. Confidence-radius formulas and the stated POR-UCBVI dimension dependence also change.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions now claim sample-complexity guarantees, improvements over naive history summarization, and exponentially sharper GOLF guarantees through HABE. This substantially extends v1's recursive-structure contribution, which relied on a specialized reward-machine learner. The framework and dueling-reduction claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 newly explains why separately learning rewards across timesteps misses recursive structure and motivates joint Q-function classes. It qualifies the improvement as requiring dense intermediate feedback and notes that HABE and BE dimensions are not universally ordered. Section 2.2 also expands the deployment-based rationale for regret versus sample complexity.

D1.justification: Appendix F adds GOLF's confidence-set update, auxiliary function-class information and a prescribed beta parameter, absent from v1. Neither version supplies an experimental implementation or code/data release.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning against history summarization and existing Bellman-eluder guarantees. Remark 3 changes the emphasis from recovering Chatterji et al.'s guarantees to improving them and adds a cardinal-versus-dueling query-complexity comparison with Wang et al.'s P-OMLE. PAC and reward-machine references are added, while the DPO discussion is removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and model exposition are extensively rewritten. Generic optimism templates move from the main text into Appendix C; the separate recursive-dynamics section becomes a model-free subsection within Section 3. The title, contribution framing and appendix organization also change.

P2.justification: v2 adds algorithm displays for generic model-free optimism, GOLF and standalone POR-UCRL/POR-UCBVI instantiations, and compacts Algorithm 1. Equations and paragraphs are reformatted, while the overall single-column presentation remains similar. Neither version contains figures or result tables.

improvement.justification: The GOLF/HABE analysis develops v1's limited treatment of recursive structure, and the reorganization improves accessibility. However, Appendix B Lemma 5 claims a high-probability guarantee for one uniformly sampled policy while its proof substitutes an average over policies. This does not establish the claim as written, and several new sample-complexity corollaries depend on it. The substantive additions and this reliability concern prevent a confident net quality judgment.
